learningObjective: Correctly define TF32 and its relationship to FP32.

canonicalClaims.claim: TF32 is a Tensor Core input format with 8-bit exponent (FP32 range) and 10-bit mantissa (FP16 precision), 19 bits total. Storage stays FP32; truncation happens at multiplier input; accumulation is FP32.
conditions: The target GPU is Ampere or newer with Tensor Core support.
A framework flag or API call enables TF32 (e.g., PyTorch `allow_tf32`).
nonImplications: Does not imply TF32 matches FP32 bit-for-bit.
Does not imply TF32 is used for every FP32 tensor without opt-in.

misconceptions.claim: TF32 equals FP32 in numerical accuracy; the name is a marketing rebrand.
misconceptions.whyWrong: TF32 truncates the mantissa to 10 bits at the multiplier input, which is observable in FP32 correctness tests.

misconceptions.claim: TF32 equals BF16 with an FP32 accumulator.
misconceptions.whyWrong: BF16 has 7-bit mantissa; TF32 has 10-bit mantissa. They differ.

misconceptions.claim: TF32 is a CPU vector format unrelated to GPU Tensor Cores.
misconceptions.whyWrong: TF32 is defined on NVIDIA Tensor Cores; CPUs do not implement it.

misconceptions.claim: TF32 always accelerates FP32 matmul without any user action.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Frameworks require an opt-in flag; some workloads disable it for numerical parity with pure FP32.

performanceScenarios: TF32 matmul on Ampere Tensor Core: roughly 8× FP32 throughput; on Hopper, roughly 16×.
